raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem

Equal-TP (MHA/GQA) PD-disaggregated KV transfer collapses bandwidth when the
decode-side KV cache becomes fragmented: each `(group, layer)` slice becomes a
separate transfer entry, and per-entry device-memory (D2H) copy overhead
dominates the transfer.

- engine-level: 1 entry → 4792 MB/s; 4096 entries → 15.5 MB/s
- end-to-end (200 concurrent long shared-prefix requests): 1.41 → 1.76 req/s
  (+25%), TPOT 23.03 → 13.80 ms (−40%)

This is the root cause behind the bandwidth collapse reported in #5450
(which was auto-closed without a confirmed fix; the "larger page-size"
workaround avoids, but does not fix, fragmentation).

## Root cause

1. `alloc_extend` allocates across non-contiguous free segments under pool
   pressure (decode-side radix cache reuse) → fragmented dst indices.
2. The equal-TP direct path (`send_kvcache`) emits one transfer entry per
   (group × layer), so fragmentation blows up the entry count.
3. Per-entry fixed cost × thousands of entries → bandwidth collapse.

## Fix

Route equal-TP fragmented chunks through the existing staging path
(local gather → 1 bulk RDMA → decode scatter), collapsing G×2L entries into 1.
Gated behind `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER` and
`SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_MIN_GROUPS` (default 8); `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_ALWAYS`
opts into staging for every equal-TP chunk.

- `mooncake/conn.py`: equal-TP fragmentation branch + `_fragmented_groups` +
  `_ensure_equal_tp_staging_req` (on-demand STAGING_REQ) + bounded spin
- `decode.py`: register gate widened to non-MLA equal-TP, excluding
  fake-transfer requests (warmup/health-check) to avoid a warmup hang
- `utils.py`: poll demote gate switched to `is_staging_room`
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_MIN_GROUPS` / `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_ALWAYS`

All changes are env-gated and default-off: behavior is unchanged unless
staging is explicitly enabled.

### Follow-up refinements (from KIOSHIROI/sglang#1, by @simple-sun)

The original implementation rounded non-last sends down to a full staging grid
so every staged chunk started on a grid boundary. That delayed the tail of a
cached prefix until later prefill work completed. The follow-up makes partial
grid pieces stageable and hardens the control paths:

- **Partial chunks with allocation-identity safety.** A grid-aligned piece may
  now stage with its actual page count (`_is_first_staging_piece`). Only the
  first piece of a grid slot stages; continuations that start inside an
  already-used slot stay on the direct path, so they can never reuse that
  slot's staging allocation.
- **Early-send overlap preserved.** Non-last sends are only grid-aligned when
  the sender reports `requires_staging_grid_alignment()` (PP>1, missing target
  info, or non-equal TP); equal-TP PP=1 direct sends keep their natural
  boundary.
- **No unnecessary splitting.** The scheduler asks the sender
  (`should_split_staging`) whether any grid-aligned piece can stage; contiguous
  direct sends are sent once, unsplit.
- **Convert the index range once.** `req_to_token` translation and
  `kv_to_page_indices` happen once per send range instead of per segment;
  segments slice the materialized page array.
- **Allocation-request synchronization.** On-demand STAGING_REQ
  deduplication/submission is serialized (`request_lock`), the dedup key is
  rolled back on send timeout, and STAGING_RSP updates are published under the
  watermark condition variable with `notify_all()` (closing the missed-wakeup
  window in the readiness wait).
- **Failure classification.** Allocation/control-request failures use a
  dedicated result (`_STAGING_REQUEST_FAILED`) and fail only the affected room
  instead of blacklisting the transport session; `send_kvcache_staged` returns
  the real transport code instead of raising, so RDMA failures follow the
  regular room/session failure path and unexpected exceptions still propagate.
- **Scope guard.** The optional equal-TP staging path is restricted to PP=1;
  other layouts keep the original conservative grid alignment.

Defaults are unchanged: staging off, `MIN_GROUPS=8`, `ALWAYS` off.

## Validation

- Warmup passes with `STAGING_BUFFER=1`, and with staging + decode radix cache
  on both MHA and GQA.
- Fragmented workload (200 rooms shared-prefix): 1.41 → 1.76 req/s (+25%),
  TPOT 23.03 → 13.80 ms (−40%), 90/90 staging transfers succeeded, 0 failures.
- Healthy path no regression (1.47 → 1.49 req/s, within noise).

Follow-up validation (TP1 prefill + TP1 decode on two H20-3e GPUs; 49,152
input tokens including 49,088 cached tokens, 1 output token; 60 samples per
condition after four warm-up requests; the second run reverses the
fragmentation-test order):

| KV layout | Run | Parent mean TTFT | Follow-up mean TTFT | Reduction |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Low fragmentation | 1 | 64.22 ms | 55.43 ms | 13.7% |
| Low fragmentation | 2 | 65.72 ms | 56.06 ms | 14.7% |
| High fragmentation | 1 | 84.05 ms | 58.41 ms | 30.5% |
| High fragmentation | 2 | 87.14 ms | 58.76 ms | 32.6% |

- Paired correctness checks matched output token IDs and logprobs; transfer
  observations confirmed staged 16,320-token partial pieces followed by direct
  64-token continuations.
- CPU contracts: 18 behavior tests in three `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_equal_tp_staging_*.py`
  files pass on the follow-up and fail on the unpatched parent (they execute
  the actual scheduler send range, partial-piece identity, direct/forced paths,
  allocation requests, waiter notification, transport return boundary, and
  worker failure handling).
- High fragmentation was constructed by permuting free slots in 16-token runs
  on an empty prefill pool: a controlled fragmentation experiment, not
  production cache aging.

### TP8 validation (2 x 8 x H20-3e, by @simple-sun)

Two hosts, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct BF16, prefill TP8 / decode TP8, PP=1,
Mooncake over RDMA (8 x 400G NICs per host). Measured on `ce78cab2`
(`c87a869b` plus the `@staticmethod` binding fix in KIOSHIROI/sglang#2): 3600
measured requests, 0 failures/timeouts; three runs with warm-up per
configuration, including reversed mode order; values are medians of per-run
metrics.

| Workload | Mode | TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | TPOT p50 (ms) | req/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Low frag (radix off, mem 0.40, 200 x 4096-token unique, 128 out, conc 100) | OFF | 5394.23 / 5455.58 | 5.296 | 15.4146 |
| Low frag | ON | 5373.88 / 5442.58 | 5.332 | 15.4146 |
| Low frag | ON-ALWAYS | 5337.53 / 5421.27 | 5.778 | 15.3714 |
| High frag (radix on, mem 0.30, 3072 shared + 5120 unique, 200 prompts, 2048 out, conc 100) | OFF | 486.85 / 10233.93 | 23.828 | 1.8460 |
| High frag | ON | 396.53 / 10239.59 | 23.830 | 1.8478 |
| High frag | ON-ALWAYS | 441.36 / 10266.96 | 23.833 | 1.8458 |

- High-frag ON: TTFT p50 -18.6% (all three paired runs improved); p90, TPOT and
  throughput unchanged. Low-frag ON stays on the direct path (0 staged
  requests, unchanged); ON-ALWAYS forces staging and costs ~9% TPOT, as expected
  for a non-default mode.
- Per-rank evidence: submitted descriptor count per run drops from 882,992 to
  19,227 (-97.8%) with identical byte counts; 91/200 high-frag requests stage
  per run, with matching decode scatter counts on all 8 ranks.
- Controlled mechanism test (49,152 input tokens, 49,088 cached, 1 output):
  OFF to ON TTFT p50 192.55 -> 78.43 ms (-59.3%), prefix-transfer API busy time
  99.11 -> 16.92 ms (-82.9%).
- Correctness: independent concurrent runs differ even OFF vs OFF, so runs were
  compared by deterministic trajectory replay (OFF record, OFF self-replay, ON
  replay, ALWAYS replay): all 200 greedy outputs, both hosts' per-rank
  trajectories, and 200 KV/recurrent-state checks per decode rank match.
- Phase timings are clock-offset-corrected cumulative timestamps (prefill
  complete -> decode handoff -> first decode compute completion), not pure RDMA
  durations.

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- GPU TP8 validation: TP8 was validated on 2x8xH20-3e (see the TP8 validation
  section above); TP>1 layouts other than TP8 are not measured. The TP1 A/B
  above is TP1 only.
- DCP × equal-TP interaction is not covered by the current regression tests
  (DCP transfer takes the pre-existing relayout branch; split segments carry
  per-segment `src_page_offset`/`num_kv_tokens`).
- Pre-existing ordering gaps reported separately (Success published before a
  deferred KV chunk transfer; transfer + CHUNK_READY possible after a
  cancellation during the readiness wait) reproduce on the parent revision and
  are tracked as follow-ups, not regressions from this change.
- Pre-RDMA local/destination staging-buffer capacity failures still return -1
  and follow the legacy session-failure path.

nodes.body: @KIOSHIROI Could you provide a detailed reproduction setup for this issue? Decode-side RadixCache is normally disabled, and I haven’t observed this problem with equal-TP transfer in end-to-end runs, so I’d like to better understand the scenario where it occurs.

Hi, thanks for the review! I reproduced it on 2× A800 80GB with mooncake TCP (MC_FORCE_TCP=1). The trigger is decode-side radix cache + memory pressure, which is why it doesn't show up in the default path.

Three things are needed together:

1. **Decode radix cache** (`--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`). With shared-prefix requests the decode side reuses shared pages, so dst pages of a transfer become non-contiguous even when src is contiguous. This is the main source of fragmentation. With radix disabled (default), dst stays contiguous and we see the healthy ~56 entries/chunk.
2. **Memory pressure + concurrency.** mem_fraction 0.3 + 200 concurrent rooms makes alloc_extend span multiple non-contiguous free segments.
3. **Equal TP** (prefill TP == decode TP). The direct path emits one entry per (group × layer), so the fragmented range gets multiplied into a large number of entries.

Repro:

```bash
MEM_FRACTION=0.3 DECODE_RADIX=1 PREFILL_NO_RADIX=1 \
  scripts/start_pd_master.sh mooncake

sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --base-url http://0.0.0.0:30000 \
  --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
  --gsp-num-groups 1 --gsp-prompts-per-group 200 \
  --gsp-system-prompt-len 64 --gsp-question-len 8000 --gsp-output-len 2048 \
  --request-rate inf
```

(shared 64-token system prompt, 8000-token questions, 2048-token outputs, 200 concurrent prompts, closed loop)

I re-ran this exact setup today. Entry count goes from ~56 to 952 per batch (up to 3976 in the worst batch of earlier logs), TPOT ~24 ms, throughput ~1.36 req/s. With DECODE_RADIX=0 the same workload keeps dst contiguous, entry count stays healthy, and no collapse — so the default config won't hit this.

I can attach the raw kv_transfer_*.jsonl logs (per-batch n_entries) if that helps.

@YAMY1234 the repro setup is in my reply above. The key trigger is decode radix cache + memory pressure: `DECODE_RADIX=1` with 200 rooms at `mem_fraction=0.3`. I re-ran it today — per-batch entries go from ~56 to 952 (worst batch 3976 in earlier logs), TPOT ~24ms. Let me know if it reproduces on your side, happy to share the raw logs.

Hi @KIOSHIROI, we built on your implementation in this PR and opened a follow-up targeting your branch: https://github.com/KIOSHIROI/sglang/pull/1.

Our incremental changes:
- Support grid-aligned partial chunks while keeping continuations within the same slot on the direct-transfer path.
- Preserve early-send overlap and avoid unnecessary splitting for direct transfers.
- Convert KV indices once before splitting.
- Improve staging allocation-request synchronization and isolate allocation failures from transport-session failures.

We compared these changes against your implementation at 72a2d68687b7 using TP1 prefill + TP1 decode on two H20-3e GPUs. Each request had 49,152 input tokens, including 49,088 cached tokens, and generated one output token. Each condition retained 60 samples after four warm-up requests.

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Low fragmentation | 1 | 64.22 ms | 55.43 ms | 13.7% |
| Low fragmentation | 2 | 65.72 ms | 56.06 ms | 14.7% |
| High fragmentation | 1 | 84.05 ms | 58.41 ms | 30.5% |
| High fragmentation | 2 | 87.14 ms | 58.76 ms | 32.6% |

The second run reversed the fragmentation test order. High fragmentation was constructed by permuting free slots in 16-token runs; these measurements cover controlled fragmentation rather than production aging.

Output token IDs and logprobs matched in the paired correctness checks. All 16 CPU behavior tests passed on each of the two hosts. Full experiment details are included in the follow-up PR.

Would you be interested in incorporating these changes into this PR?

Thanks for the detailed protocol. I have completed the TP8 runs on two 8×H20 hosts with Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct BF16, TP8/PP1 on both sides, and Mooncake RDMA using eight available 400G NICs per host.

I used c87a869b with one local fix shared by all modes: adding the missing @staticmethod to _is_first_staging_piece. OFF / ON (MIN_GROUPS=8) / ON-ALWAYS used the requested settings and a 4096 MiB staging pool.

The low-fragmentation workload used decode radix off, mem fraction 0.40, 200 unique 4096-token prompts, 128 output tokens, concurrency 100. The high-fragmentation workload used decode radix on, mem fraction 0.30, a 3072-token shared prefix plus 5120-token unique suffix, 200 prompts, 2048 output tokens, concurrency 100. No allocator permutation was used for these runs.

Each configuration had three measured runs with warm-up, including reversed mode order. Values below are medians of the three per-run metrics, not pooled-request percentiles. All 3600 measured requests succeeded, with zero failures/timeouts.

| Workload | Mode | TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | TPOT p50 (ms) | req/s |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Low fragmentation | OFF | 5394.23 / 5455.58 | 5.296 | 15.4146 |
| Low fragmentation | ON | 5373.88 / 5442.58 | 5.332 | 15.4146 |
| Low fragmentation | ON-ALWAYS | 5337.53 / 5421.27 | 5.778 | 15.3714 |
| High fragmentation | OFF | 486.85 / 10233.93 | 23.828 | 1.8460 |
| High fragmentation | ON | 396.53 / 10239.59 | 23.830 | 1.8478 |
| High fragmentation | ON-ALWAYS | 441.36 / 10266.96 | 23.833 | 1.8458 |

High-fragmentation ON reduces TTFT p50 by 18.6%; all three paired runs improved. TTFT p90, TPOT, and throughput remain approximately unchanged. Low-fragmentation ON stays on the direct path and is approximately unchanged.

Per-rank evidence: high-fragmentation ON stages 91/200 requests per run, with matching decode scatter counts on all eight ranks. The median total submitted descriptor count per rank per run drops from 882,992 (OFF) to 19,227 (ON), a 97.8% reduction, with identical submitted byte counts. ON-ALWAYS stages all 200 requests. Low-fragmentation ON stages none.

For the cross-host phase measurement, I corrected clock offsets before/after each run and recorded prefill completion, decode handoff, and the first decode compute-result event. High-fragmentation p50 prefill-complete→handoff is 16.713 / 15.604 / 61.080 ms for OFF / ON / ALWAYS; prefill-complete→first decode compute completion is 61.608 / 61.085 / 76.866 ms. The latter endpoint is the first token computed by decode, distinct from the prefill-generated token and client TTFT; these are cumulative phase times, not pure RDMA durations.

For correctness, independent concurrent runs do have output differences, including OFF vs OFF. I therefore separately recorded and replayed the actual engine trajectory, rather than only fixing request submission order. For each workload I ran OFF record → OFF self-replay → ON replay → ALWAYS replay. Each replay matches all 200 complete greedy outputs, both hosts' per-rank trajectories, and 200 KV/recurrent-state checks per decode rank. The high workload reaches an actual decode batch of 100; the low workload reaches 20. No reference-token forcing was used, and replay timings are excluded from the performance table. The additional c1 checks also match for both workloads.

As a separate controlled mechanism test, I repeated the fragmented hot-prefix setup with the corrected multi-NIC configuration: 49,152 input tokens, 49,088 cached on prefill, one output token, and artificial 16-token contiguous source-page runs. Across three runs, OFF→ON TTFT p50 falls from 192.55 to 78.43 ms (−59.3%), and prefix transfer API busy time from 99.11 to 16.92 ms (−82.9%). This is supplemental evidence for fragmented transfers, not a replacement for your requested workload or a physical link-bandwidth measurement.

detail.body:
## Problem

Equal-TP (MHA/GQA) PD-disaggregated KV transfer collapses bandwidth when the
decode-side KV cache becomes fragmented: each `(group, layer)` slice becomes a
separate transfer entry, and per-entry device-memory (D2H) copy overhead
dominates the transfer.

- engine-level: 1 entry → 4792 MB/s; 4096 entries → 15.5 MB/s
- end-to-end (200 concurrent long shared-prefix requests): 1.41 → 1.76 req/s
  (+25%), TPOT 23.03 → 13.80 ms (−40%)

This is the root cause behind the bandwidth collapse reported in #5450
(which was auto-closed without a confirmed fix; the "larger page-size"
workaround avoids, but does not fix, fragmentation).

## Root cause

1. `alloc_extend` allocates across non-contiguous free segments under pool
   pressure (decode-side radix cache reuse) → fragmented dst indices.
2. The equal-TP direct path (`send_kvcache`) emits one transfer entry per
   (group × layer), so fragmentation blows up the entry count.
3. Per-entry fixed cost × thousands of entries → bandwidth collapse.

## Fix

Route equal-TP fragmented chunks through the existing staging path
(local gather → 1 bulk RDMA → decode scatter), collapsing G×2L entries into 1.
Gated behind `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER` and
`SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_MIN_GROUPS` (default 8); `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_ALWAYS`
opts into staging for every equal-TP chunk.

- `mooncake/conn.py`: equal-TP fragmentation branch + `_fragmented_groups` +
  `_ensure_equal_tp_staging_req` (on-demand STAGING_REQ) + bounded spin
- `decode.py`: register gate widened to non-MLA equal-TP, excluding
  fake-transfer requests (warmup/health-check) to avoid a warmup hang
- `utils.py`: poll demote gate switched to `is_staging_room`
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_MIN_GROUPS` / `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_ALWAYS`

All changes are env-gated and default-off: behavior is unchanged unless
staging is explicitly enabled.

### Follow-up refinements (from KIOSHIROI/sglang#1, by @simple-sun)

The original implementation rounded non-last sends down to a full staging grid
so every staged chunk started on a grid boundary. That delayed the tail of a
cached prefix until later prefill work completed. The follow-up makes partial
grid pieces stageable and hardens the control paths:

- **Partial chunks with allocation-identity safety.** A grid-aligned piece may
  now stage with its actual page count (`_is_first_staging_piece`). Only the
  first piece of a grid slot stages; continuations that start inside an
  already-used slot stay on the direct path, so they can never reuse that
  slot's staging allocation.
- **Early-send overlap preserved.** Non-last sends are only grid-aligned when
  the sender reports `requires_staging_grid_alignment()` (PP>1, missing target
  info, or non-equal TP); equal-TP PP=1 direct sends keep their natural
  boundary.
- **No unnecessary splitting.** The scheduler asks the sender
  (`should_split_staging`) whether any grid-aligned piece can stage; contiguous
  direct sends are sent once, unsplit.
- **Convert the index range once.** `req_to_token` translation and
  `kv_to_page_indices` happen once per send range instead of per segment;
  segments slice the materialized page array.
- **Allocation-request synchronization.** On-demand STAGING_REQ
  deduplication/submission is serialized (`request_lock`), the dedup key is
  rolled back on send timeout, and STAGING_RSP updates are published under the
  watermark condition variable with `notify_all()` (closing the missed-wakeup
  window in the readiness wait).
- **Failure classification.** Allocation/control-request failures use a
  dedicated result (`_STAGING_REQUEST_FAILED`) and fail only the affected room
  instead of blacklisting the transport session; `send_kvcache_staged` returns
  the real transport code instead of raising, so RDMA failures follow the
  regular room/session failure path and unexpected exceptions still propagate.
- **Scope guard.** The optional equal-TP staging path is restricted to PP=1;
  other layouts keep the original conservative grid alignment.

Defaults are unchanged: staging off, `MIN_GROUPS=8`, `ALWAYS` off.

## Validation

- Warmup passes with `STAGING_BUFFER=1`, and with staging + decode radix cache
  on both MHA and GQA.
- Fragmented workload (200 rooms shared-prefix): 1.41 → 1.76 req/s (+25%),
  TPOT 23.03 → 13.80 ms (−40%), 90/90 staging transfers succeeded, 0 failures.
- Healthy path no regression (1.47 → 1.49 req/s, within noise).

Follow-up validation (TP1 prefill + TP1 decode on two H20-3e GPUs; 49,152
input tokens including 49,088 cached tokens, 1 output token; 60 samples per
condition after four warm-up requests; the second run reverses the
fragmentation-test order):

| KV layout | Run | Parent mean TTFT | Follow-up mean TTFT | Reduction |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Low fragmentation | 1 | 64.22 ms | 55.43 ms | 13.7% |
| Low fragmentation | 2 | 65.72 ms | 56.06 ms | 14.7% |
| High fragmentation | 1 | 84.05 ms | 58.41 ms | 30.5% |
| High fragmentation | 2 | 87.14 ms | 58.76 ms | 32.6% |

- Paired correctness checks matched output token IDs and logprobs; transfer
  observations confirmed staged 16,320-token partial pieces followed by direct
  64-token continuations.
- CPU contracts: 18 behavior tests in three `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_equal_tp_staging_*.py`
  files pass on the follow-up and fail on the unpatched parent (they execute
  the actual scheduler send range, partial-piece identity, direct/forced paths,
  allocation requests, waiter notification, transport return boundary, and
  worker failure handling).
- High fragmentation was constructed by permuting free slots in 16-token runs
  on an empty prefill pool: a controlled fragmentation experiment, not
  production cache aging.

### TP8 validation (2 x 8 x H20-3e, by @simple-sun)

Two hosts, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct BF16, prefill TP8 / decode TP8, PP=1,
Mooncake over RDMA (8 x 400G NICs per host). Measured on `ce78cab2`
(`c87a869b` plus the `@staticmethod` binding fix in KIOSHIROI/sglang#2): 3600
measured requests, 0 failures/timeouts; three runs with warm-up per
configuration, including reversed mode order; values are medians of per-run
metrics.

| Workload | Mode | TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | TPOT p50 (ms) | req/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Low frag (radix off, mem 0.40, 200 x 4096-token unique, 128 out, conc 100) | OFF | 5394.23 / 5455.58 | 5.296 | 15.4146 |
| Low frag | ON | 5373.88 / 5442.58 | 5.332 | 15.4146 |
| Low frag | ON-ALWAYS | 5337.53 / 5421.27 | 5.778 | 15.3714 |
| High frag (radix on, mem 0.30, 3072 shared + 5120 unique, 200 prompts, 2048 out, conc 100) | OFF | 486.85 / 10233.93 | 23.828 | 1.8460 |
| High frag | ON | 396.53 / 10239.59 | 23.830 | 1.8478 |
| High frag | ON-ALWAYS | 441.36 / 10266.96 | 23.833 | 1.8458 |

- High-frag ON: TTFT p50 -18.6% (all three paired runs improved); p90, TPOT and
  throughput unchanged. Low-frag ON stays on the direct path (0 staged
  requests, unchanged); ON-ALWAYS forces staging and costs ~9% TPOT, as expected
  for a non-default mode.
- Per-rank evidence: submitted descriptor count per run drops from 882,992 to
  19,227 (-97.8%) with identical byte counts; 91/200 high-frag requests stage
  per run, with matching decode scatter counts on all 8 ranks.
- Controlled mechanism test (49,152 input tokens, 49,088 cached, 1 output):
  OFF to ON TTFT p50 192.55 -> 78.43 ms (-59.3%), prefix-transfer API busy time
  99.11 -> 16.92 ms (-82.9%).
- Correctness: independent concurrent runs differ even OFF vs OFF, so runs were
  compared by deterministic trajectory replay (OFF record, OFF self-replay, ON
  replay, ALWAYS replay): all 200 greedy outputs, both hosts' per-rank
  trajectories, and 200 KV/recurrent-state checks per decode rank match.
- Phase timings are clock-offset-corrected cumulative timestamps (prefill
  complete -> decode handoff -> first decode compute completion), not pure RDMA
  durations.

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- GPU TP8 validation: TP8 was validated on 2x8xH20-3e (see the TP8 validation
  section above); TP>1 layouts other than TP8 are not measured. The TP1 A/B
  above is TP1 only.
- DCP × equal-TP interaction is not covered by the current regression tests
  (DCP transfer takes the pre-existing relayout branch; split segments carry
  per-segment `src_page_offset`/`num_kv_tokens`).
- Pre-existing ordering gaps reported separately (Success published before a
  deferred KV chunk transfer; transfer + CHUNK_READY possible after a
  cancellation during the readiness wait) reproduce on the parent revision and
  are tracked as follow-ups, not regressions from this change.
- Pre-RDMA local/destination staging-buffer capacity failures still return -1
  and follow the legacy session-failure path.

Hi, thanks for the review! I reproduced it on 2× A800 80GB with mooncake TCP (MC_FORCE_TCP=1). The trigger is decode-side radix cache + memory pressure, which is why it doesn't show up in the default path.

Three things are needed together:

1. **Decode radix cache** (`--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`). With shared-prefix requests the decode side reuses shared pages, so dst pages of a transfer become non-contiguous even when src is contiguous. This is the main source of fragmentation. With radix disabled (default), dst stays contiguous and we see the healthy ~56 entries/chunk.
2. **Memory pressure + concurrency.** mem_fraction 0.3 + 200 concurrent rooms makes alloc_extend span multiple non-contiguous free segments.
3. **Equal TP** (prefill TP == decode TP). The direct path emits one entry per (group × layer), so the fragmented range gets multiplied into a large number of entries.

Repro:

```bash
MEM_FRACTION=0.3 DECODE_RADIX=1 PREFILL_NO_RADIX=1 \
  scripts/start_pd_master.sh mooncake

sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --base-url http://0.0.0.0:30000 \
  --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
  --gsp-num-groups 1 --gsp-prompts-per-group 200 \
  --gsp-system-prompt-len 64 --gsp-question-len 8000 --gsp-output-len 2048 \
  --request-rate inf
```

(shared 64-token system prompt, 8000-token questions, 2048-token outputs, 200 concurrent prompts, closed loop)

I re-ran this exact setup today. Entry count goes from ~56 to 952 per batch (up to 3976 in the worst batch of earlier logs), TPOT ~24 ms, throughput ~1.36 req/s. With DECODE_RADIX=0 the same workload keeps dst contiguous, entry count stays healthy, and no collapse — so the default config won't hit this.

I can attach the raw kv_transfer_*.jsonl logs (per-batch n_entries) if that helps.

Thanks for the detailed protocol. I have completed the TP8 runs on two 8×H20 hosts with Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct BF16, TP8/PP1 on both sides, and Mooncake RDMA using eight available 400G NICs per host.

I used c87a869b with one local fix shared by all modes: adding the missing @staticmethod to _is_first_staging_piece. OFF / ON (MIN_GROUPS=8) / ON-ALWAYS used the requested settings and a 4096 MiB staging pool.

The low-fragmentation workload used decode radix off, mem fraction 0.40, 200 unique 4096-token prompts, 128 output tokens, concurrency 100. The high-fragmentation workload used decode radix on, mem fraction 0.30, a 3072-token shared prefix plus 5120-token unique suffix, 200 prompts, 2048 output tokens, concurrency 100. No allocator permutation was used for these runs.

Each configuration had three measured runs with warm-up, including reversed mode order. Values below are medians of the three per-run metrics, not pooled-request percentiles. All 3600 measured requests succeeded, with zero failures/timeouts.

| Workload | Mode | TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | TPOT p50 (ms) | req/s |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Low fragmentation | OFF | 5394.23 / 5455.58 | 5.296 | 15.4146 |
| Low fragmentation | ON | 5373.88 / 5442.58 | 5.332 | 15.4146 |
| Low fragmentation | ON-ALWAYS | 5337.53 / 5421.27 | 5.778 | 15.3714 |
| High fragmentation | OFF | 486.85 / 10233.93 | 23.828 | 1.8460 |
| High fragmentation | ON | 396.53 / 10239.59 | 23.830 | 1.8478 |
| High fragmentation | ON-ALWAYS | 441.36 / 10266.96 | 23.833 | 1.8458 |

High-fragmentation ON reduces TTFT p50 by 18.6%; all three paired runs improved. TTFT p90, TPOT, and throughput remain approximately unchanged. Low-fragmentation ON stays on the direct path and is approximately unchanged.

Per-rank evidence: high-fragmentation ON stages 91/200 requests per run, with matching decode scatter counts on all eight ranks. The median total submitted descriptor count per rank per run drops from 882,992 (OFF) to 19,227 (ON), a 97.8% reduction, with identical submitted byte counts. ON-ALWAYS stages all 200 requests. Low-fragmentation ON stages none.

For the cross-host phase measurement, I corrected clock offsets before/after each run and recorded prefill completion, decode handoff, and the first decode compute-result event. High-fragmentation p50 prefill-complete→handoff is 16.713 / 15.604 / 61.080 ms for OFF / ON / ALWAYS; prefill-complete→first decode compute completion is 61.608 / 61.085 / 76.866 ms. The latter endpoint is the first token computed by decode, distinct from the prefill-generated token and client TTFT; these are cumulative phase times, not pure RDMA durations.

For correctness, independent concurrent runs do have output differences, including OFF vs OFF. I therefore separately recorded and replayed the actual engine trajectory, rather than only fixing request submission order. For each workload I ran OFF record → OFF self-replay → ON replay → ALWAYS replay. Each replay matches all 200 complete greedy outputs, both hosts' per-rank trajectories, and 200 KV/recurrent-state checks per decode rank. The high workload reaches an actual decode batch of 100; the low workload reaches 20. No reference-token forcing was used, and replay timings are excluded from the performance table. The additional c1 checks also match for both workloads.

As a separate controlled mechanism test, I repeated the fragmented hot-prefix setup with the corrected multi-NIC configuration: 49,152 input tokens, 49,088 cached on prefill, one output token, and artificial 16-token contiguous source-page runs. Across three runs, OFF→ON TTFT p50 falls from 192.55 to 78.43 ms (−59.3%), and prefix transfer API busy time from 99.11 to 16.92 ms (−82.9%). This is supplemental evidence for fragmented transfers, not a replacement for your requested workload or a physical link-bandwidth measurement.
